Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a widened mediastinum with an indistinct aortic knob, which is a classic radiographic sign suggestive of traumatic aortic injury (specifically at the isthmus) in the context of blunt trauma or crush accidents. While pediatric patients can have a prominent thymus, the clinical history of significant trauma makes ruling out vascular injury the priority based on this finding.
